title: How the build's sessions are organized: a coordinator per repo
why: Orchestrator, Oct 28 14:58 CDT: you proposed three tiers (coordinator, lane leads, triage, all Opus); an Opus blind review with web research says the shape is sound but the cut is wrong.
note: Waits on waiting-page item 50 (pick a recommended). The review: one coordinator per repo, not one for all repos, since batches, CI and the question page are per repo. Triage becomes a planner the coordinator starts on demand and stays the only roadmap writer; the coordinator owns the repo's question page, so shiv faces one writer. Lane sessions run Sonnet, build themselves and spawn a fresh reviewer; Opus only on round 3 or the coordinator's flag (Anthropic's gain came from an Opus lead over Sonnet workers). Before starting lanes the coordinator records which files each lane owns and runs overlapping lanes one after another; it checks the head sha and CI on GitHub before batching. One name for the coordinator in GLOSSARY.md, retiring orchestrator, point guard (degen) and arbiter (q_max). Sources: Anthropic's multi-agent research system, Building effective agents, Claude Code subagents and agent-teams docs, Cognition's two multi-agent posts. No build until shiv answers. Port: yes, every repo with standing roles. Placed after c200 (triage 12, Oct 28).
